rationale: 'Shall' duty in a regulation to establish and maintain a risk management process for high-risk AI; enforced through provider obligations (Art 16) and penalties in Art 99 rather than in Art 9 itself.

Binding 'shall' duty; data governance practices (procedural) and quality standards for training/validation/testing data (substantive) serve system quality and testing, though a Risk Assessment reading (bias examination) is arguable; sanctions via Art 99.
Binding design requirement (substantive) plus provision of instructions for use to deployers (reporting/disclosure); principal purpose is transparency; sanctions via Art 99.

Binding design requirement enabling effective human oversight; coded Accountability as oversight allocates human control/responsibility, though Safety is a plausible alternative; sanctions via Art 99.
Binding performance standard for accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity across the lifecycle; sanctions via Art 99.

Ministry guidelines without statutory force; imperative phrasing in a list of guidelines for industry is an expectation, not a legal duty; publication of transparency reports is a reporting measure with no enforcement route.

Recommendation to government to design proportionate, graded obligations across the value chain (institutional direction; content concerns substantive obligations); it frames a future regime rather than imposing a compliance duty.
Recommendation that authorities develop an India-specific risk classification framework; framework-building, not a compliance duty.
'Should' assigns testing/evaluation and advisory functions to the AI Safety Institute; institution-building provision.

'Should' allocates monitoring and enforcement leadership to sectoral regulators; principal purpose is enforcement allocation, and it structures the institutional framework rather than imposing a compliance duty (System-level only is arguable).

Due diligence rules made under the IT Act are binding; duties to deploy technical measures (substantive) and to label/embed provenance metadata in synthetic content (disclosure); non-compliance consequence is in Rule 7 (loss of s.79 safe harbour).

Binding rule stating the consequence of non-observance (loss of s.79(1) safe-harbour immunity); it is a consequence rule rather than a conduct duty, hence nature Other; the provision itself states the consequence, so Direct.
White paper principle phrased with 'should', non-statutory; to be applied by existing regulators within their remits, so enforcement depends on their general powers.
Non-statutory 'should' principle requiring governance measures and clear lines of accountability (institutional allocation and substantive standard); relies on existing regulators.
Government's own undertaking to deliver a central risk-register function in support of regulators; builds a central function rather than imposing a compliance duty.

Non-statutory 'should' principle on robust, secure and safe functioning (substantive) with continual risk identification/management (procedural); primary purpose safety; relies on existing regulators.

Describes government's own approach of issuing principles non-statutorily for regulators to apply within remits; concerns implementation/enforcement architecture rather than imposing a duty (System-level only arguable).
Government request (not a legal requirement) that regulators publish updates on implementing the principles, aimed at public visibility; no compliance route attaches.

Policy expectation about possible future mandatory design interventions for highly capable GPAI; creates no present obligation, so force Not specified; dimension inferred from focus on design of advanced models.
OECD Council Recommendation, 'should commit to' transparency and responsible disclosure (disclosure plus conduct standard); no enforcement mechanism.
'Should be accountable' principle in a non-binding recommendation; no enforcement route.
'Should' apply systematic risk management across lifecycle (process requirement); no enforcement route.
'Should' be robust, secure and safe - an outcome standard; no enforcement route.

Council instruction to the Digital Policy Committee, binding within OECD internal procedure, to report on implementation (reporting) assigned to a committee (institutional); a follow-up/review mechanism rather than a compliance duty on AI actors; dimension could alternatively be Transparency or Enforcement.
